gaps.sentence: It was the first time she ___ a car on her own.
gaps.hint: it was the first time takes past perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It was the first time' in past contexts, English uses the past perfect: had driven.

gaps.sentence: I ___ what the problem is, so let me explain it to the others.
gaps.hint: see meaning understand is a state
gaps.explanation: When 'see' means 'understand', it is a state verb and cannot be continuous: see.

gaps.sentence: I ___ coffee at all, but I drink tea every morning.
gaps.hint: a general habit contrasted with another habit
gaps.explanation: A permanent habit takes the present simple, so the negative form is: don't drink.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ across the desert.
gaps.hint: action in progress at a future time
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' — future continuous for an ongoing future action.

gaps.sentence: Every morning she ___ an hour in the garden before breakfast.
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' marks a repeated routine, which takes the present simple: spends.

gaps.sentence: At midnight, the protesters ___ outside the parliament, refusing to move.
gaps.hint: at midnight, in progress at that point
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific past moment takes the past continuous: were standing.

gaps.sentence: Look — someone ___ that vase; it is in pieces on the floor.
gaps.hint: look plus a visible present result
gaps.explanation: The present result of a very recent action takes the present perfect: has broken.

gaps.sentence: This time tomorrow I ___ my driving test.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future time takes the future continuous: will be taking.
